review.summary:
Design and statistics review of docs/research/protocols/merge_vv.md (v0). Read only; no simulation. All numbers below come from the stored E30 rows (streamed once), docs/research/results/c1/checks.json, the run-commit code, and the NGSIM CSV; scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5b1/2d269ac5-95be-4f04-801b-ec9cc9873355/scratchpad/vvr/design/ (a1-a4.py/.out for the E30 rows, ng1-ng2.py/.out for NGSIM). My re-implementation of the C-D5 statistic reproduces the stored reading (lr400_16_1: +9.93, SE 1.92, 97.5 % interval [+6.24, +14.95] at B = 8,000, against screen.json +9.934, SE 1.942, [+6.161, +14.971]).

Verdict: the plan is not ready for approval. One blocker and seven majors.

Blocker: V3 cannot answer Q3 as designed. Its stop gate and its HOLDS reading pull against each other. In E30, 84-87 % of the close-following is at the two merges, and away from them v3w is behind lr400_16_1 (-8.6 %). If the gate passes, C1 check (a) says merge close-following falls by 66-98 %, so the 600-m total is mostly the away part. A simple no-artefact model on the E30 rows (merge counts scaled equally in both arms) predicts an edge against lr400_16_1 of +7.3 % (merges x 0.34), +4.7 % (x 0.2), +0.4 % (x 0.1), -5.6 % (x 0.02), with HOLDS probabilities about 0.85, 0.3, 0.01 and 0. The likely reading is NOT SHOWN, which the draft itself says tells nothing; REVERSED could appear with no artefact at all. V3 measures dependence on lane length; whether that dependence is an artefact has to come from V4 (do real drivers stop like this) and V5.

Majors: (1) the stop gate is a point rule with no defined statistic, applies to all 9 arms, and has no E30 or merge-1 evidence behind its 80 %; a failure voids about 8,640 runs. (2) V2 tests replication on fresh seeds, not resolution, and the E1 meter uses a different TTC definition (no minGap) from ttc_net. (3) The 98.75 % level is not needed for the both-must-pass readings, the 1.9 % null bar belongs to 97.5 % intervals, and the power line uses z = 2.24, which is the 97.5 % value. (4) n = 480 resolves an edge of about +6.8 to +7.3 % with power 0.9; the edges expected at 600 m are smaller. (5) V4's PLAUSIBLE rule fails a perfectly realistic plant about 29 % of the time per quantity, the 6 samples are really 2 sites, and at I-80 the lane-change definition gives one fixed merge point for all vehicles. (6) V1's 0-of-20 inspection only bounds non-events below 14 %, more than the 9.9 % edge it defends, and criterion 3 recomputes from the counter's own log. (7) How the frozen policy reads position at 600 m is not fixed; with positions from the built network, merge 2 sits 300 m beyond where it was in training.

Useful facts found in the stored rows, no runs needed: the 1-Hz count sampled half a second later (ttc_half) gives the same edge (difference +0.50 points, SE 0.34; correlation 0.999 per arm); the edge is not made of samples just after a lane change (edge without them +10.5 % [+6.6, +15.5]); v3w has 31 % fewer lane-end stopped vehicle-seconds than lr400_16_1 [+24.6, +38.8], and merge 1 has 137-257 of them per run in E30 (14.5-37 in S), so merge 1 is not clean in E30.

Limits of this review: the scaling model is an inference, not a measurement; the NGSIM pass is rough (raw speeds, lane numbering from my recollection of the NGSIM documentation, not verified, periods split by time); I did not read V5's sources.

findings.title: V3 cannot separate an artefact from 'longer lanes remove the merge close-following for every arm'; its likely reading is NOT SHOWN
findings.claim: V3's gate and its HOLDS reading work against each other. The gate needs lane-end stops to fall by 80 %. When they do, merge close-following falls too, and the 600-m total becomes mostly the away-from-merges part, where v3w is behind lr400_16_1. So a plant with no artefact at all is expected to read NOT SHOWN, and can read REVERSED. The draft says NOT SHOWN tells nothing, and REVERSED would be recorded as 'the edge exists only with 300-m lanes', which a committee will hear as 'artefact'. V3 measures dependence on lane length, not whether the 300-m behaviour is an artefact.
findings.evidence: E30 rows at 300 m (a1.out): median close-following per run for lr400_16_1 is 1,219, of which merge 1 265.5, merge 2 741, away 155.5; v3w learners 1,000-1,092, of which away 132.5-183.5. Away edge against lr400_16_1 -8.6 % [-14.5, -1.5] (a3.out; screen.json -8.6 [-14.7, -1.4]). C1 check (a) in S (checks.json): at 595 m merge-2 close-following fell 66 % (no control) and 98 % (p333), with stops down 90.8 % and 99.4 %. Model on the E30 rows, merge counts multiplied by k in both arms, away unchanged (a3.out; an inference, not a measurement): against lr400_16_1 the edge is +7.3 % at k = 0.34, +4.7 % at 0.2, +0.4 % at 0.1, -5.6 % at 0.02; P(lower bound above 0) about 0.84-0.89, 0.28-0.38, 0.01-0.02, 0; P(REVERSED) 0.33 at k = 0.02. Against grid_lr400_13_1 the edge stays positive (+18.5 to +7.5). Real count noise at lower counts would make power lower than the model says.
findings.fix: Reword Q3 and V3 as dependence: 'does the edge depend on the acceleration-lane length?'. Never word an outcome as artefact or not; say in section 0 that artefact against mechanism is answered by V4 (do field drivers stop before merging at a comparable traffic state) and V5, with V3 as the size of the dependence. Add an expectations paragraph before data, as c1_confirm.md section 2 did, with the model table above. Replace the outcomes by: HOLDS (both lower bounds above 0); NO EDGE AT 600 m, NOT WORSE (not HOLDS, and both lower bounds above -5 %, the project's harm margin); WORSE (an upper bound below 0). Record for the last two: 'with 600-m lanes merge close-following fell by x % for the rules and y % for v3w; what is left is mostly away from the merges, where v3w is not better than lr400_16_1 (V531)'. Add to the deciding print, fixed now: the merge-area edge (3a, ramp 1, 4a, ramp 2 groups) in events per run and in %, at both lengths, and the fall in merge close-following per arm, so the committee sees how much lane length does compared with control.

findings.title: The stop gate is a point rule with no defined statistic, covers all 9 arms, and its 80 % has no E30 or merge-1 evidence
findings.claim: The gate can fail under no effect, so it is a real gate. But (a) 'fall by at least 80 % (median of paired differences)' does not say what the percentage is of, and has no interval; (b) 'for every arm' lets no control or p333, which are context arms, void the reading of the deciding arms; (c) whether 600 m passes in E30 cannot be said from the stored data, and a failure is found only after about 8,640 runs; (d) a pass at exactly 80 % still leaves 120-245 stopped vehicle-seconds per run, more than merge 1 had in S.
findings.evidence: end_stop and end_stop2 count stopped vehicle-seconds (speed below 1 m/s in the last 30 m, sampled each second; plant_sweep.py:338-341), not stops. E30 medians at 300 m of end_stop + end_stop2 (a3.out): v3w 608-722, lr400_16_1 1,120, grid_lr400_13_1 1,225.5, p333 1,181, no control 816; 20 % of these is 122-245. Merge 1 alone in E30: 137-257 per run, against 14.5 (no control) and 37 (p333) in S (checks.json 'printed'). So merge 1 in E30 is 6-14 times S, and no length check exists for merge 1 or for E30 at any length. In S the response is steep: no control's end_stop2 was 526.5 at 295 m, 523 at 445 m, 48.5 at 595 m (a 90.8 % fall, 11 points above the bar). Random halves of one arm give a cut in median stops of about -15 % to +13 % (a4.out), so 80 % is far from noise. Precedent: V512 defined binding as the 95 % lower bound of the cut in median end_stop2 (paired ratio of medians) of at least 50 %, for the deciding arms and no control; V513 added a pick step because a late 'did not bind' was the likely outcome.
findings.fix: Gate statistic, as V512: cut = 1 - median(stops at 600 m) / median(stops at 300 m) on the same seeds, seeds resampled jointly, 95 % lower bound; per merge (end_stop and end_stop2 separately) and for the sum. Gate on the 7 deciding arms and no control; p333 printed. Keep 80 % only if the author wants 'mostly removed'; print the residual in vehicle-seconds per run beside it. Add a pilot before the bulk run, C1's pilot form: about 40 seeds x {300, 600} m x {w1u500, lr400_16_1, grid_lr400_13_1, no control} = 320 runs; the script prints only the stop cuts and the SEs of the edges, never an edge. If a cut's lower bound is below the bar, the author decides (stop, or another length) before the 600-m bulk is spent. Write 'stopped vehicle-seconds' everywhere instead of 'lane-end stops', and let V1 report how many vehicles stop and for how long.

findings.title: V2 tests replication on fresh seeds, not whether 1 Hz is enough; the 0.1-s meter also uses another TTC definition
findings.claim: V2 reads MET if the 0.1-s edge has both lower bounds above 0 on fresh seeds. If 1 Hz is adequate, that outcome depends only on whether E30 replicates. If 1 Hz is not adequate, for example the 0.1-s edge is half the 1-Hz edge, V2 still reads MET more often than not. A failure would be worded 'the 1-Hz edge is not shown at 0.1 s' even when the 1-Hz edge itself failed to replicate. The criterion has no null. And the meter does not count what ttc_net counts.
findings.evidence: Power of 'lower bound above 0' at n = 480, SE 1.92 (a3.out): true edge +9.9 gives 0.996-0.998; true edge +5 gives 0.55-0.64. e1_meter.py:70-74 takes gap = lead[1]; the counter uses gap = lead[1] + getMinGap (plant_sweep.py:222, b_env.py:811), so the meter's 1-Hz count will not equal ttc_net. The draft has no criterion that the meter's 1-Hz count equals the row's ttc_net. Stored rows already bear on the question: ttc_half (the same count taken half a second later) correlates 0.999 with ttc_net per arm, the ratio of sums is 0.996-1.001, and the edge differs by +0.50 points (SE 0.34) for lr400_16_1 and -0.26 (SE 0.36) for grid_lr400_13_1 (a3.out). The paired difference of two edges from the same runs is therefore about 5 times more precise than an edge.
findings.fix: V2 criteria: (1) the meter uses the counter's definition (gap + minGap), and its 1-Hz count equals ttc_net exactly in every run (else BUG); (2) deciding statistic: edge at 0.1 s minus edge at 1 Hz, same runs, C-D5 form, 95 % interval, with a sign-flip null printed; MET if the interval lies within +/-3 points (about half of E30's lower bound of 6.2; the author may pick another margin now) for both rules; LIMIT otherwise, with both edges printed. (3) Print the share of 0.1-s close-following time that the 1-Hz count misses, per arm. With this statistic about 120 seeds at 300 m are enough (SE about 0.7 by scaling 0.34-0.36 from 480); it need not run at 600 m. State the ttc_half result now in the record as partial evidence for PR-23. Separately, state how the fresh-seed 300-m 1-Hz reading is reported if it does not show the edge (see D9).

findings.title: Interval level, null bar and the power line do not match each other or the CF convention
findings.claim: V2 and V3 use 98.75 % intervals 'Bonferroni over the 2 rules' for readings that need both lower bounds above 0. A both-must-pass reading needs no correction; c1_confirm.md says so itself ('PASS needs every test to pass, so no correction is needed'). The correction is needed only for REVERSED, which fires on any one upper bound. The draft then pairs 98.75 % intervals with a null bar of 1.9 %, which is the bar for 97.5 % intervals. The power line uses z = 2.24, which is the 97.5 % value. V2 names no null at all.
findings.evidence: read_cf.py:25-26: MAIN pct (1.25, 98.75) with bar 0.019; EXT pct (0.625, 99.375) with bar 0.0094 and 20,000 swaps. So the project's bar is 1.5 x the nominal tail: 1.9 % for 97.5 % intervals, 0.94 % for 98.75 %. z for a 0.625 % tail is 2.50, for 1.25 % it is 2.24. Recomputed power at n = 480, SE 1.92 (a3.out): at +9.9, 0.998 (z 2.24) or 0.996 (z 2.50); at +5, 0.64 or 0.55. The draft's 'about 0.6' matches z 2.24, not the 98.75 % interval it names.
findings.fix: HOLDS and V2's MET: 97.5 % lower bounds, both must be above 0, swap null bar 1.9 % with 2,000 swaps (re-estimated once with 20,000 if above), exactly as CF. WORSE/REVERSED: 98.75 % upper bounds (either rule), null bar 0.94 % with 20,000 swaps. State the error rates in one paragraph: a false HOLDS at most 1.25 %, a false MET at most 1.25 %, together at most 2.5 %; a false WORSE at most 1.25 %. Correct the power line with the level actually used.

findings.title: n = 480 is sized for the 300-m edge; at 600 m the expected edges are smaller and the SE is unknown. Fewer seeds do not suffice for the 600-m reading, but do for the 300-m half
findings.claim: The draft's SE of about 1.9 points is right for 300 m. It carries to 600 m only if counts stay as large and as steady, which the gate is meant to prevent. At n = 480 the reading resolves an edge of about +6.8 to +7.3 % with power 0.9; the model in D1 puts the 600-m edge against lr400_16_1 between +7.3 and -5.6. The 300-m half does not need 480 seeds for anything that decides.
findings.evidence: SE of E(lr400_16_1) by resampling n seeds from the 480 (a3.out): 1.92 at 480, 2.36 at 320, 2.73 at 240, 3.31 at 160, 3.86 at 120. For grid_lr400_13_1: 2.20, 2.63, 3.03, 3.64, 4.20. Power of 'lower bound above 0' at a true +9.9 with 97.5 % bounds: 0.998, 0.976, 0.918, 0.775, 0.631. Smallest edge with power 0.9 at n = 480: (2.24 + 1.28) x 1.92 = 6.8 % at 97.5 %, (2.50 + 1.28) x 1.92 = 7.3 % at 98.75 %. For a true +5 % with power 0.9 the SE must be 1.42, about 880 seeds (about 1,010 at 98.75 %), by SE proportional to 1/sqrt(n). Under the model the SE in % grows as merge counts shrink: 2.09 at k = 0.34, 2.43 at 0.2, 2.72 at 0.02.
findings.fix: Fix n for the 600-m half by a rule written now and fed by the pilot of D2 (SEs only): the smallest n in {480, 720, 960} at which a true edge of +5 % against lr400_16_1 has power 0.8 with 97.5 % bounds; if none does, run 960 and state the resolvable edge in the record. The cost is not binding (about $0.14 per 1,000 runs). The 300-m half can drop to 120 seeds if the author wants to save hours: the gate (cuts of 80 % against noise of about 15 %) and V2's paired difference (D3) are both well resolved there; say then that the 300-m edge at n = 120 is printed only (SE about 3.9). Keeping 480 at both lengths is simpler and also acceptable; then say what the 300-m reading is for (D9).

findings.title: V4's PLAUSIBLE rule fails a realistic plant about 29 % of the time per quantity, rests on 2 sites, and one quantity is degenerate at I-80
findings.claim: The rule can fail, but mostly for the wrong reasons. (1) If the plant were a seventh field sample from the same population, its median would fall inside the range of the other six with probability 5/7 = 0.71; all four quantities inside, about 0.26 if independent. (2) The six samples are two sites times three periods, so the range is the gap between two sites: wide where the sites differ (any plant value passes), narrow where they agree (a small difference fails). (3) The share of stopped mergers is set by how congested the site is, not by how drivers merge. (4) With merges defined as lane-ID changes, every I-80 merge falls at the same point.
findings.evidence: Rough extraction from the NGSIM CSV (ng2.out; raw speeds, lane numbering from my recollection of the NGSIM documentation [VERIFY], periods split by time): 1,000 on-ramp merges, 104-130 per US-101 period, 207-221 per I-80 period. Merge position as a share of the lane: I-80 1.012, 1.012, 1.011 with bootstrap SE 0.000 (the lane label ends at one fixed point); US-101 0.24, 0.29, 0.35; range [0.24, 1.01]. Share below 1 m/s in the 10 s before: I-80 12.1, 14.0, 15.3 %; US-101 0, 0, 0.8 %; between-site gap 13.5 points against 0.8-3.2 within a site. Median merge speed: I-80 4.2-5.8 m/s, US-101 11.0-13.8 m/s. Median lag time gap 1.06-1.48 s, with per-period bootstrap SE 0.06-0.12 s. Leave-one-out on the field alone: a real period lies inside the range of the other five in 18 of 24 cases (4 of 6 for lag gap and for merge speed).
findings.fix: Replace the rule, with everything below fixed and committed before the plant's merge log is read. (1) Define a merge by the vehicle's lateral crossing of the lane boundary (Local_X), not by the Lane_ID change, and verify lane lengths in the documentation; drop 'merge position as a share of the lane' as a labelled quantity unless the lane types match (US-101 is an auxiliary lane ending at an off-ramp). (2) Compare at a matched traffic state: bands of target-lane speed at the merge (for example below 5, 5-10, above 10 m/s); a plant band is compared only with field bands holding at least 30 merges, otherwise 'no field counterpart'. (3) Per quantity and band, tolerance = the envelope of the site-period values widened on each side by the largest within-site spread; commit the envelope and its leave-one-out false-OUTSIDE rate, and use the label only where that rate is at most 1 in 6; otherwise the quantity is descriptive. (4) Labels SIMILAR or DIFFERENT with the direction stated (plant stops more, accepts shorter gaps); never 'validated'. (5) Make the stopped-merger share and the accepted lag gap the two headline quantities, since they carry Q3 (D1). (6) Plant side: human mergers with a human follower read separately from those with an ALKS follower, and the same table printed for lr400_16_1 and w1u500, because the claim compares arms with 0.8-1.2 s ALKS headways, not no control.

findings.title: V1's random inspection is too small to bound non-events below the size of the edge, and criterion 3 checks the counter against its own log
findings.claim: Criterion 4 inspects 40 samples, 20 at the merges. Finding none bounds the non-event share only below 14 % there, while the edge to defend is 9.9 %. The 40 are drawn from 12 traced runs at two lengths and three arms, so the 300-m E30 arms get a handful each, and samples within a run are clustered (one closing pair is counted on several consecutive seconds). Criterion 3 recomputes TTC from the gap and speeds the counter itself logged, so it cannot find a wrong leader. No criterion covers end_stop, although the plan's gate rests on it.
findings.evidence: 95 % upper bound for 0 found in n: 1 - 0.05^(1/n) = 13.9 % for n = 20, 7.2 % for n = 40. Edge against lr400_16_1: 9.9 %, 121 events per run of 1,219 (a2.out, a3.out). A traced run holds about 1,000-1,800 counted samples (a1.out medians), so all of them can be classified by code. The runner already has a raw trace of both acceleration lanes for an offline recount of end_stop (plant_sweep.py etrace, 'M2 section 7 PR-24').
findings.fix: Replace criteria 3 and 4. (3) Independent recount: the tracer writes, each second, the raw state of every vehicle (id, type, lane, lane position, speed, length, minGap); an offline script finds each vehicle's leader on its own lane from positions alone, recounts TTC below 3 s, and lists every sample where it and the counter disagree (junctions, lane ends, a leader on the next edge, a leader mid lane change). Same for end_stop and end_stop2, plus the number of vehicles that stop and their stop durations. (4) Every counted sample is classified by code into fixed classes: same-lane pair; leader stopped in the last 30 m of an acceleration lane; follower on an acceleration lane; pair in a junction; disagreement with the recount; double count of one follower in one second. Shares per arm at 300 m, with the 2 seeds shown separately. MET if double counts are 0 and the disagreement share is at most 1 % in every arm; LIMIT naming the class otherwise. The visual check stays, drawn from the disagreement set first and then at random per arm at 300 m, reported with its bound ('0 of n, so below 3/n'). Carry the classes as split counters in all V3 runs at 300 m and print the edge per class on the full seed set: that locates the edge by lane (PR-28) and says how much of it is followers closing on a vehicle stopped at the lane end. Consider tracing two stored E30 seeds instead of fresh ones: the stored row is then the untraced twin and the trace is of the claim's own runs.

findings.title: How the frozen policy reads position at 600 m is not fixed, and the natural choice moves merge 2 by 300 m in the policy's own coordinates
findings.claim: The draft says the policy's position inputs are 'recomputed from the built network'. With that choice the policy sees merge 2 where edge 4 was in training, half of each longer lane reads as 'past the merge', and the last part of the road is clipped. Another mapping (the lanes rescaled to the trained coordinates) is equally defensible and may give another result. The choice must be made, with its reason, before data; otherwise it is a free choice after the fact, and NOT SHOWN cannot be read.
findings.evidence: b_env.py:894-901: x is 0 at the start of 3a and adds real lane lengths; 4a starts at len(3a) + len(3), which is about 1,489 m as built and about 1,789 m with a 600-m 3a. b_env.py:929: the inputs are clip(x/1000, -3.5, 3.3) and clip(x/300, -1, 1). The second saturates at 300 m, so the second half of a 600-m 3a reads as beyond the lane. The road downstream of the 3a start is about 3.28 km as built and about 3.88 km with both lanes at 600 m, so the last 580 m read as 3.3. The two rules of V3 are LocalRule (200-m speed bins ahead, b_env.py:994-1022) and need only a bin count per edge, so they adapt cleanly; the handicap is one-sided.
findings.fix: Add a decision VV-D7 with both options and a recommendation. Option A (built coordinates): simplest, the policy is furthest from training. Option B (trained coordinates): each lengthened lane mapped linearly onto its trained 295 m and everything downstream shifted back, so merges start and end where the policy learned them. Whichever is chosen, state it in the record sentence, and print how many of the policy's decisions at 600 m had a position input outside the range seen at 300 m. If the author wants both, B decides and A is printed; say so now.

findings.title: The fresh-seed 300-m reading is a second replication with no reporting rule
findings.claim: V3 re-runs 300 m on 480 fresh seeds and prints the edge as 'never deciding'. If the true edge is nearer the stored lower bound than the point, that reading can fail to show an edge, and the plan does not say how the two readings are then reported.
findings.evidence: P(lower bound above 0 at n = 480, SE 1.92, 97.5 %) is 0.998 at a true +9.9 and 0.84 at a true +6.2, the stored lower bound (normal approximation; my computation).
findings.fix: State now: the 300-m reading on the fresh seeds is reported beside V530 whatever it shows, with the pooled estimate over both seed sets (960 seeds) printed; V530's reading is not replaced. Read the 600-m result only as 'at 600 m', never as a change from 300 m, unless the difference of the two edges on the same seeds is printed with its interval.

findings.title: HOLDS is worded as 'does not depend on the 300-m lanes' and 'the closest rules'
findings.claim: A positive edge at 600 m does not show independence of lane length: the edge may halve. And only 2 of the 26 non-learning arms run at 600 m, chosen as closest at 300 m; another rule may be closest at 600 m.
findings.evidence: The two rules are the closest away from the merges at 300 m (screen.json: -8.6 % and +4.6 %; next lr400_13_2 +15.7 %, lr1000_16_2 +16.6 %), which supports the choice but not the word 'closest' at 600 m.

review.summary: Build reviewer (label build). The plan can be built, and E30's own plant can be left untouched, but the build section is wrong or silent on several things that would quietly spoil V3 and V2. (1) corridor.build with accel_len=600 in r2m3 does not shorten edge 3, as the plan says. It moves nodes ae and d but not the r2m3 nodes. With accel_len=accel2_len=600 you get 3a=600, edge 3=1,200 (kept), 4a=300 (not 600) and a ramp-2 connector rj2 of 330 m instead of 30 m. With accel2_len left at 300, 4a has zero length. (2) The plan's geometry goal contradicts itself: if 3a grows downstream, you cannot keep both the merge spacing and edges 3-5. (3) The policy's positions already come from the built network in every E30 arm, and the policy was trained with fix_x. So 'recompute, identity at 300' holds trivially for the policy. The real problem is that its inputs stay inside the training range but point to the wrong place: everything past 3a shifts by 300 m, and x above 3.3 km is clipped. The plan's 'beyond its training range' wording is wrong, and a remap must be chosen before any data. (4) LocalRule.N_BINS is hard-coded. At 600 m both lr400 rules would never see the last 195 m of 3a and 4a, without any error. Bins worked out from the network match the hard-coded values exactly at 300 m (checked). (5) The e1_meter measures TTC with SUMO's gap without minGap and samples its 1-Hz reading 0.1 s off ttc_net's sampling times. It has never been wired into a run. (6) ttc_net, conflicts() ttc3, m_ttc3_all and the sum of m_road_ttc3 agree on all 14,880 rows because they are computed in the same pass, at the same moment, from the same getLeader(v, 200) call and formula. They are not independent checks, so V1 criterion 2 can only confirm the wiring. (7) The V3 gate adds end_stop and end_stop2 together, so merge 1 (the author's question) can stay unresolved. Both counters are vehicle-seconds, not stops. Cost: the 9 V3 arms average 99.4 s of wall time per run in the stored rows, which matches the plan's rate. The 0.1-s meter (about 6.2 M extra getLeader calls per run) and the 11 % longer lanes are not costed. findings.title: V1 tracer: where to hook it, which calls are forbidden (V386), and what getLeader does at a lane end
findings.claim: Hooks: ttc samples inside conflicts() (plant_sweep.py:212), with the extra fields read by getters only. Lane-end samples: the existing trace_end/etrace already logs every vehicle on 3a_0 and 4a_0 each second with position and speed (plant_sweep.py:331-336, M2 §7 PR-24), so reuse it rather than writing a new one. Merges: the 1-Hz trackers (plant_sweep sec() road_lane/accel_t; measure.py merge_pos) see a merge up to 1 s late, so the gap accepted at the merge has to be logged at step level. In step(), after warm-up, compare the vehicle sets of ls.lane.getLastStepVehicleIDs('3a_0'/'4a_0') between steps. For each vehicle that left, log its last lane-0 position and, at its first step on lane 1, getLeader/getFollower(v, 200) plus speeds. Keep a 10-s per-vehicle speed history for 'minimum speed before'. Forbidden from the tracer: env._x (writes xlast, b_env.py:875/891, the V386 effect), env._obs, env._v2v/_smooth/_ease, any rule's __call__ (ZonePattern writes self.last), meas.decisions. env._x_base() is safe (fills once from lane lengths). Lane end, from source reading and to be confirmed by the trace: 3a_0 and 4a_0 have no outgoing link, so getLeaderOnConsecutive stops at the lane end. The front vehicle on an acceleration lane has no leader and is never counted; its closing followers are. Lane changes are instantaneous here (no sublane, no lanechange.duration), so a leader on another lane should not occur. I may be wrong on edge cases such as partial vehicles.

review.summary:
Committee-member review of docs/research/protocols/merge_vv.md (draft v0). Read only; nothing edited. No simulations run. Every number below comes from stored E30 rows, the NGSIM CSV or code at c1c 4dfefca, through scripts in /tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5b1/2d269ac5-95be-4f04-801b-ec9cc9873355/scratchpad/vvr/committee/ (agg.py, band.py, rate.py, nodes.py, ng1-ng4.py, with their .json outputs).

Verdict: no blocker. The draft asks the right five questions, but as written it would probably leave Q3 (lane length) without an answer and could mislead on Q4 (merge behaviour). There are 8 major findings:
1. In V3, the outcome NOT SHOWN cannot be interpreted, and it is the likely outcome. The edge sits at merge 2 (in stored rows, against lr400_16_1, the 4a part of the median paired difference is 101 of 128 counted samples). Away from both merges the policy is worse (-10 %). C1 check (a) found that merge-2 close-following almost disappears at 595 m.
2. The V3 HOLDS sentence ("does not depend on the 300-m lanes") claims more than one extra length can show.
3. The V4 criterion ("plant median within the range of the 6 field medians") has no null and mostly measures how the NGSIM lanes are coded:
   - US-101 lane 7 to 6 is the gore, where the on-ramp lane is renamed: 90 % of these changes fall between 188 and 201 m.
   - On I-80, 78 % of lane 7 to 6 changes sit at the coded end of lane 7.
   - The field range is wide: share of merging cars that crawled (below 1 m/s) in the 10 s before merging is 0.5 % on US-101 and 14 % on I-80.
4. "Lane-end stops" are vehicle-seconds of standing, not counts of stops. Merge 1 is not small in E30: medians of 136-310 vehicle-seconds per run, against the 7 per run from baseline v2 that the record cites. V3's 80 % gate may not be reachable.
5. V1 criterion 4 can hardly fail by construction: SUMO's getLeader looks only at the same lane, and each follower has one leader. The doubtful categories (crawling in queues, standing at a lane end) have no criterion.
6. The measure is longitudinal, same-lane TTC. Lane changes are instantaneous (no lanechange.duration option anywhere in v5b). In stored rows the edge over lr400_16_1 is not shown for samples within 5 s of a lane change. So the claim is about close following inside the merge areas, not about merge conflicts, and should be worded that way.
7. How ALKS behaves at merges (merging from ramps under LC2013 with lcCooperative 1; R157 scope) is a committee question the draft never addresses.
8. The 300-m readings in V2 and V3 are a fresh-seed replication of E30. How they will be worded must be fixed before data.

Points in the author's favour, from stored data:
- The two independent counters, ttc3 and ttc_net, are equal in all 14,880 rows.
- The SUMO 1.27.1 source confirms that getLeader's gap leaves out the follower's minGap, so gap + minGap is the bumper gap.
- Against lr400_16_1 the edge also appears with the follower at 10 m/s or faster: +9.6 %, paired CI on the difference [17.4, 45.8] samples. This is descriptive, post hoc and uncorrected.
- The merge areas run congested, as the NGSIM sites do:
  - mean speed on 4a_1: 6.3 m/s with no control, 9.4 m/s with lr400_16_1;
  - median mainline speed in the raw NGSIM data: 10.6 m/s on US-101 lane 5, 5.6 m/s on I-80 lane 6.
- The counted quantity's base rate is of the same order in the plant and the field:
  - plant, per vehicle-second on edges 3a and 4a: 0.8-1.9 %;
  - NGSIM main lanes, raw speeds: 1.5 % on US-101, 3.2 % on I-80.

The single extra check that would most change a committee's confidence: a pre-registered split of every counted sample at 300 m, run in V3's fresh-seed runs with a read-only counter. It splits by lane (acceleration lane or main lane), by whether the leader is standing in the last 30 m of an acceleration lane, by time since a merge, and by follower speed. The edge would then be re-read on main-lane samples that have no standing leader at the lane end. This answers the artefact question without changing the geometry and without the policy leaving its training range, which is what makes NOT SHOWN uninterpretable in V3.

Literature named below is a pointer only, marked [VERIFY]: I have not read any of it in full.

The edge over the closest rule lives mostly on edge 4a, and C1 check (a) showed merge-2 close-following almost vanishing at 595 m. Away from both merges the policy is worse. findings.claim:
SUMO's getLeader returns only a vehicle on the same lane, or on its best-lane continuation, and each follower has at most one leader per sample. So 'a leader on another lane' and 'counted twice' are almost impossible by construction. The samples a committee will doubt are all admitted by the definition and are only printed:
- crawling in a queue at low speed;
- approaching a vehicle standing at a lane end.
The trace as designed will read MET almost surely.

findings.title: Claim wording: same-lane close-following in merge areas, not merge conflicts
findings.claim: Lane changes in this plant are instantaneous: no lanechange.duration, no sublane model. TTC is longitudinal and same-lane. A merge therefore enters the count only after the jump, as a same-lane follower sample. In stored rows the edge over lr400_16_1 is not shown on samples within 5 s of a lane change; it sits in plain car-following inside the merge areas. 'Fewer close calls at merges' would be heard as fewer merge conflicts, which the plant does not measure.

findings.title: V4's 6-sample PLAUSIBLE rule cannot answer Q4 and has no null
findings.claim: The rule 'plant median within the range of the 6 field medians' is not a workable criterion. (1) It is 2 sites with 3 back-to-back periods each, not 6 samples: within a site the medians are nearly equal, so the range is the difference between two sites. (2) No null was computed (project rule). By arithmetic, a value exchangeable with n field values falls outside their range with probability 2/(n+1): 0.29 for n = 6, 0.67 for n = 2. A field-like plant would read OUTSIDE on at least one of four quantities most of the time. (3) Where the sites differ, the rule cannot fail. (4) Where they agree, the range is as narrow as one median's sampling interval, so the verdict depends on field noise and the extraction rule. (5) One quantity is a share and one median is defined only for closing pairs, so 'median' does not apply as written. Scope: this blocks V4, not V1-V3.
findings.evidence: Exploratory, before protocol approval. p4.log and p5.log in the scratch folder. Merge position share per period: US-101 0.226, 0.294, 0.347; I-80 1.002, 1.001, 1.001 (label rule); stored plant no control 0.41 (3a) and 0.49 (4a), all vehicle classes (q2.log), inside trivially. Lag time gap medians 1.175, 1.169, 1.063, 1.20, 1.35, 1.21 s, each with a bootstrap 95 % interval about 0.25-0.45 s wide, against a range 0.29 s wide. The I-80 medians move to 1.36, 1.33, 1.27 s with the lateral rule at 72.5 ft and to 1.25, 1.43, 1.48 s at 74.5 ft. The 2/(n+1) figure is my derivation, not a computed result.

findings.title: At I-80 the Lane_ID change is not the merge
findings.claim: The draft extracts merges 'as lane changes from the on-ramp or auxiliary lane into the adjacent main lane'. findings.title: Merge position 'as a share of the lane length' has no comparable denominator
findings.claim: The three geometries differ in kind. The plant has a 294.72 m parallel lane with a hard end. US-101 has an auxiliary lane of about 650-700 ft (198-213 m as seen in the data) that continues into an off-ramp, so nothing forces a merge by its end. I-80 has an angled ramp and taper with no parallel section, whose start lies outside the camera view. A share of lane length depends on start and end points that the data do not give for I-80 and that mean something different at US-101.
findings.evidence: Exploratory. p3.log: US-101 7->6 label change at Local_Y 615-662 ft (median 653), 6->8 at 1,310-1,356 ft (median 1,347); 3 of 402 on-ramp tracks left by the off-ramp and 40 lane changes go 8->5. I-80: on-ramp tracks first appear at a median 333 ft; lane-7 median Local_X falls steadily from 96.5 to 76.7 ft over Local_Y 100-650 ft; lateral crossings run to p95 798 ft. Plant lane length: c1_t0.len_4a_0 = 294.72 in the stored rows. The endpoints I used (655-1,310 ft and 333-666 ft) are my assumptions.
findings.fix: Drop merge position as a judged quantity. If kept, report it in metres from a documented reference point, for US-101 only, as description, with the geometry difference stated beside it. Get the lane lengths and lane lines from the NGSIM site documentation and mark them [VERIFY] until read.

findings.title: The 10-s stop share is censored, threshold-sensitive, and measures queue stops at I-80
findings.claim: 'Share of merging vehicles below 1 m/s in the 10 s before merging' cannot be computed robustly from NGSIM and would not compare like with like. (1) Many merging vehicles are in view for less than 10 s before merging. (2) The share moves with the speed definition and threshold. (3) US-101 has none. (4) I-80's stops are part of a crawling queue on both lanes, spread along the whole ramp, not waits at a lane end beside moving traffic, which is the plant behaviour in question.
findings.evidence: Exploratory. p4.log: share of merges with 10 s of track before the merge is 0.277, 0.402, 0.472 at US-101 and 0.663, 0.904, 0.918 at I-80. Stop share at I-80: 0.111, 0.148, 0.144 on raw speed and 0.058, 0.134, 0.115 on the 1-s central difference; at a 2 m/s threshold 0.28-0.51 (p5.log); US-101 0 in all periods (smoothed). p6.log: 198 of 611 I-80 ramp vehicles have a 1-Hz sample below 1 m/s before crossing; those samples sit at a median Local_Y of 487 ft, with 30.6 % in the last 100 ft; lane-6 traffic within 30 m moves at a median 1.17 m/s, and 1.3 % of the stopped samples are beside traffic above 5 m/s. Plant no control (q2.log): run-mean speed on the main lane beside the acceleration lane is 10.67 m/s (3a_1) and 6.33 m/s (4a_1).
findings.fix: Replace the 10-s window with quantities read at the merge instant, which need no window: merger speed minus target-lane follower speed (median, and the share more than 3 m/s slower), and the share merging below 2 m/s while the follower is above 5 m/s ('standing merge beside moving traffic'). Field first look: median difference +0.4 to +1.15 m/s; share more than 3 m/s slower 0-2.6 %. Say in the protocol that neither site shows lane-end waiting beside moving traffic, so the field data can bound it but not reproduce it.

findings.title: The follower TTC median at merge is not robust in the field data
findings.claim: TTC of the target-lane follower exists only when the follower is closing, which is 23-32 % of merges. A per-period median then rests on 32-65 pairs and its interval is wider than any plant-field difference worth reading. The share below 3 s rests on 0-7 events per period.
findings.evidence: Exploratory. p5.log: closing pairs per period 35, 36, 32 (US-101) and 58, 53, 65 (I-80); medians 20.4, 21.0, 13.9, 14.9, 19.9, 11.0 s with bootstrap 95 % intervals such as 12.1-35.2 s and 7.6-14.4 s; TTC < 3 s counts 0, 1, 3, 3, 1, 7 (smoothed speed) and 0, 1, 3, 3, 2, 9 (raw v_Vel).
findings.fix: Do not judge a TTC median. Report, per site pooled, the share of merges with follower TTC below 3 s, with its count and an exact binomial interval (15 events in 1,001 merges over both sites). State that it is too rare in the field to carry a verdict. Keep the accepted lag time gap as the main quantity.

findings.title: Extraction details the draft should fix in writing
findings.claim: Several data facts change counts if left open: exact duplicate rows; reused vehicle ids; no period column; motorcycles; too few trucks for the draft's 'cars and trucks'; clipped accelerations; noisy raw speeds.
findings.evidence: Exploratory. p1.log: 704,000 exact duplicates at US-101, 0 at I-80. p2.log and p3.log: 2,847 and 3,001 distinct Vehicle_ID against 6,101 and 5,678 tracks; (Vehicle_ID, Total_Frames) alone merges 1 and 4 pairs; |v_Acc| at 11.2 ft/s2 in 5.7 % and 8.9 % of rows. p4.log: merging motorcycles 5 and 4, trucks 2 and 8; raw v_Vel minus the 1-s central difference at the merge has p05/p95 of about -0.95/+0.95 ft/s; 10 merged tracks per site later return to a side lane.

(3) Periods by local clock at the merge instant: US-101 cut at 08:05 and 08:20; I-80 the 16:00 block, then cut at 17:15. (4) On-ramp vehicle = a track first seen on lane 7; motorcycles (v_Class 1) out; trucks counted but not read. (5) Speed = Local_Y difference over +/- 0.5 s; v_Acc unused. (6) Merge instant as in F2. (7) Follower = the merger's Following id at that frame, accepted only if the follower's Preceding is the merger; net lag gap = merger Local_Y minus v_length minus follower Local_Y (Local_Y as the vehicle front [VERIFY]); time gap only for follower speed above 1 m/s, excluded and negative gaps printed.
